1a20346c83.q: Why should boutique owners avoid immediately discounting slow-selling inventory after launch?
1a20346c83.a: Sometimes a product doesn't need a discount, it just needs better marketing. Before immediately marking pieces down, get creative by styling them differently, bundling something, pairing a slower top with a best-selling jean, featuring it on a live, or making it part of a themed collection. Inventory sitting around forever costs money by taking up space on racks and website, and tying up capital that could go toward new products.

c64ee9843c.q: How should organic marketing and paid advertising work together to sell through boutique inventory?
c64ee9843c.a: Organic marketing and paid ads should work together. Paid ads can do heavy lifting by continuing to get products in front of customers who visited that product, added it to their cart, engaged with your content, or have shopped on your website. Just because you have seen something 15 times doesn't mean your customer has—social media isn't showing every post to every follower and email list isn't opening every email, so you have to keep showing up with it.

60ad7dd16b.q: What should boutique owners focus on instead of panic-discounting inventory two weeks after launch?
60ad7dd16b.a: Instead of panic-marking everything at 40% off two weeks after launch, decide ahead of time how long you're willing to give inventory valuable space in your business and what you'll do at every stage. The goal is to have an exit strategy rather than panic. Ordering inventory isn't the strategy—selling through it is.
